findings.title: TypeError when Google Meet is the location and there is no destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is null or `[]`. Many callers in this PR now pass `[]`, and handleNewBooking passes `null`. The next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. Any booking whose location is Google Meet and whose user has no destination calendar now throws inside `EventManager.create`. Previously this case fell back to Cal Video. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
findings.body: Before: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`. After: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`. Video results from `createMeeting` carry a `credentialId`, which is now dropped. handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set. As a result, Zoom/Teams/etc. meetings for new bookings are orphaned on cancellation. Keep `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results too.

findings.title: Destinations without credentialId: externalCalendarId lost and team members' calendars resolved against the organizer's credentials
findings.body:
For a destination with no `credentialId` (legacy rows), the code calls `createEvent(c, event)` without `destination.externalId`. The resulting reference therefore stores no `externalCalendarId`; previously it stored `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Later updates and deletes then can't target the right calendar.

The credentials are also taken from `this.calendarCredentials`, which holds only the organizer's credentials. If a collective team member's destination calendar lacks a credentialId, an extra event is created in every organizer calendar of that integration type. The organizer gets duplicates and the team member gets nothing.

findings.title: updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId
findings.body: The references now use `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. For calendar results these come from `CalendarManager.updateEvent`, which returns neither field. editLocation persists these as new booking references with null `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId`. Previously both fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar`. Later cancellation or reschedule then falls into the legacy path or targets the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Missing credential for one host's reference makes the whole reschedule throw
findings.body: When a reference's credential is in neither `this.calendarCredentials` nor the DB (for example, a team member removed their calendar app), `credential` is `undefined`. It is still passed to `updateEvent`, which dereferences `credential.appName` and rejects. `return Promise.all(result)` is not awaited inside the `try`, so the `catch` never sees the rejection and the whole reschedule fails. Now that every host's reference is processed, this is much easier to hit. Skip references without a resolved credential.

findings.title: Rescheduling with newBookingId deletes only the first old calendar event
findings.body: The update loop now handles one calendar reference per host. The old-event cleanup still uses `booking.references.find(...)`, so it deletes only the first old calendar reference. For collective bookings, every other host keeps a stale event at the old time in their calendar.

findings.title: Error message built but no longer logged in updateAllCalendarEvents
findings.body: `console.error(message)` was removed. `message` is still computed and then unused. Failures updating calendar events are now swallowed silently and only appear as generic `success: false` results, which makes production issues hard to diagnose.

findings.title: Google createEvent ignores destination calendars without credentialId
findings.body: The calendar is now chosen only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`, with fallback to "primary". Legacy destination calendars with a null `credentialId` used to have their `externalId` respected. They now silently get events written to the primary calendar instead of the user's configured destination calendar.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses a possibly undefined calendarId
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` used to be guaranteed to be a string (`"primary"` fallback). It is now `undefined` whenever no destination matches the credential, and only the insert call applies `|| "primary"`. The follow-up `calendar.events.patch({ calendarId: selectedCalendar, ... })` then gets `undefined` and fails, so the Meet link is never written into the description. The patch promise is not awaited or caught, so the failure is an unhandled rejection.

findings.title: Google updateEvent fallback can never match, so calendarId becomes undefined
findings.body: The fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`. It runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it can never match and always yields `undefined`. Before, it fell back to the destination calendar's externalId. Updating bookings whose reference has no `externalCalendarId` (older bookings, or the paths above that now drop it) sends `calendarId: undefined` to Google and fails.

findings.title: Google deleteEvent fallback is dead code; events in non-primary calendars aren't deleted
findings.body: The same impossible `find(cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is used when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it always falls through to "primary". If the event lives in a non-primary destination calendar, Google returns 404. The code resolves 404 silently, so the cancelled booking's event stays on the user's calendar.

findings.title: Non-Google services always use the main host's calendar id, so multi-host only works for Google
findings.body: EventManager calls `createEvent` once per host's credential, but Office365 (and Lark in the same way) always uses `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, the main host's calendar. For a second host with Outlook, the request goes to `/me/calendars/<main host calendar id>/events` with the second host's token and fails. The PR's stated goal that every host with any calendar app gets the event is not met for these providers. Pick the destination matching the credential, as the Google service does.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent silently creates nothing for secondary hosts
findings.body: The calendars are filtered by the main host's destination `externalId`. A secondary host's CalDAV account never contains that URL, so the filter yields zero calendars. `Promise.all([])` succeeds, and `createEvent` returns success with a uid. A booking reference is stored for an event that was never created, and the host gets nothing in their calendar.

findings.title: Collective hosts' calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then does nothing, so every other host's destination calendar is discarded. Initialize to `[]`, or assign `teamDestinationCalendars` when the value is null.

findings.title: Unrelated loadUsers rewrite drops organization select and changes error semantics
findings.body: The dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { slug }`, so dynamic group bookings lose the organizer's org data that was previously loaded. The rewrite also turns an empty or invalid `dynamicUserList` into a generic 500 "Unable to load users" and re-wraps any HttpError as 400, discarding its original status code. These behavior changes are outside the PR's scope and untested.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation repeats per reference and misses other hosts' events
findings.body: The recurring-series deletion block now sits inside the `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. With N calendar references it runs N times. Each run iterates all organizer credentials and deletes the first calendar reference of each updated booking, sending redundant API calls. It still uses only the organizer's credentials and only the first reference per booking. For collective recurring bookings, the other hosts' events are never deleted.

findings.title: Confirmation and payment flows build evt with only one destination calendar
findings.body: Only handleNewBooking adds the collective hosts' destination calendars. Paths that create calendar events later rebuild `evt` with only the booking's or organizer's destination calendar: confirm.handler → handleConfirmation, and the Stripe/PayPal webhooks → `EventManager.create`. Collective events that require confirmation or payment still create the event only on the main host's calendar, so issue #7754 remains for those flows.

findings.title: Webhook payload `destinationCalendar` changes from object to array (breaking)
findings.body: `CalendarEvent` is spread directly into webhook payloads (BOOKING_CREATED, CANCELLED, REJECTED, etc.). `destinationCalendar` changes from an object or null to an array. It is also inconsistent across triggers: `null` from handleNewBooking but `[]` from other paths, as the e2e test now expects. This breaks third-party webhook consumers, contradicting the PR's 'non-breaking' claim, and needs a migration note or payload compatibility shim.

findings.title: Organization slug logic inverted
findings.body: The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`, which sets the slug directly only when billing is disabled. The new code is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which inverts it. Without team billing (for example, self-hosted), organizations are now created with no slug at all. With billing enabled, the slug is claimed immediately alongside `requestedSlug`, bypassing the payment flow. This unrelated change should be reverted.

findings.title: Multi-destination create/update/delete paths have no tests
findings.body: The PR changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and rewrites `createAllCalendarEvents`, `updateAllCalendarEvents` and the cancel-booking deletion loop to iterate multiple references and credentials. The PR states no tests were added. The regressions above (Meet crash on empty array, dead fallback lookups, dropped credentialId on references) would be caught by basic unit tests of these paths.
